intent:
The operator asked (2026-10-16) that kmctl support more harnesses than Claude Code through APM (Microsoft's Agent Package Manager, `apm-cli` 0.33.0), with `kmctl plugin install` kept as a thin wrapper around APM, and hooks, rules, skills and agents all delivered. This is the first of three tickets in the `multi-harness` epic (then `antigravity-harness`, then `kmctl-doctor`). It does the Claude Code harness only, on the new package layout.

Measured on 2026-10-16 in this tree:

- Harnesses kmctl installs into: 1 (Claude Code), through two routes that each deliver part of it. `kmctl plugin install` (`src/kmctl/plugin.py`) gives the 7 skills, the agent and the hook, and 0 of the 4 knowledge rules; the APM package `apm/apm.yml` gives the same, also 0 of 4 rules. The rules come only from a third step, `kmctl init` (`src/kmctl/scaffold.py`, from `src/kmctl/repo_rules/okf-bundle.md` and its 3 siblings). So a repository needs 2 commands to get the 13 items (7 skills, 1 agent, 4 rules, 1 hook); after this ticket it needs 1, and the same package can serve a second harness in the next ticket.
- `plugin/` holds 24 files. 37 tracked files outside `plugin/` and `.loop/` name `plugin/`, the plugin manifest, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `_plugin` or `repo_rules`; each is updated or removed here.

What changes:

- **The package.** Everything in `plugin/` moves under `apm/.apm/`: the 7 skill folders (with their evals) to apm/.apm/skills/NAME/, and `plugin/agents/kmctl-auditor.md` to apm/.apm/agents/ under the same name, both moved unchanged. The 4 rules move from `src/kmctl/repo_rules/` to `new:apm/.apm/instructions/okf-bundle.instructions.md`, `new:apm/.apm/instructions/docs-layout.instructions.md`, `new:apm/.apm/instructions/diagrams-stay-current.instructions.md` and `new:apm/.apm/instructions/manifesto-invariants.instructions.md`, with `paths: [...]` front matter rewritten as APM's `applyTo:` (a comma-joined string, the form jasperhg90/skills uses). Bodies stay as they are. `apm/apm.yml` drops the `{git: parent, path: plugin}` dependency and keeps `scaccogatto/okf-skills` pinned to its commit. `plugin/` (including `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` and `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` are deleted.
- **One version source.** `apm/apm.yml`'s `version:` replaces `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` as the one place the version is written: `pyproject.toml`'s hatch regex reads it, `scripts/release.py` `set` writes it and copies it to the root `apm.yml`, `current` reads it, and `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `.github/workflows/release-tag.yml` watch and commit it instead of the manifest. `scripts/check_wheel.py` and `scripts/smoke_wheel.py` check the new package data.
- **Package data.** The wheel no longer carries a plugin to stage. It carries the skills folder only, because `kmctl briefing` lists the skills it ships (`skills_dir()` in `src/kmctl/plugin.py`, read by `src/kmctl/briefing.py`): `pyproject.toml`'s force-include maps `apm/.apm/skills` instead of `plugin`, and the marketplace entry goes.
- **The hook leaves the package.** `kmctl plugin install` writes the SessionStart hook itself. For Claude it merges one SessionStart entry, with the same command, description and timeout as `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` today, into the repository's `.claude/settings.json`. It finds its own entry by the `kmctl briefing` command and replaces it in place, and leaves every other key and hook alone. ADR 0004 (one hook, never blocks) still holds; I1's test in `tests/test_plugin.py` checks the command kmctl writes instead of `hooks.json`.
- **okf's MCP server for Claude.** APM does not declare it: okf-skills is a dependency of the kmctl package, and APM skips a dependency's own MCP server unless the consumer passes `--trust-transitive-mcp` (spike:apm-only-install/1 printed only that warning and wrote no `.mcp.json`); okf's entry also points at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, which only a Claude plugin fills in. So kmctl declares it, like the hook: it merges one server, `okf-bundle`, into the repository's `.mcp.json` (`claude mcp add-json okf-bundle ... --scope user` at user scope), keeping other servers. The server runs as `uv run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scaccogatto/okf-skills/<sha>/servers/okf_mcp.py <bundle>` (spike:antigravity-harness/1: it starts from the URL and lists its three tools when given the `.okf` folder), where `<sha>` is the pin in `apm/apm.yml`, checked by a no-network test. `<bundle>` comes from a short POSIX `sh -c` launcher that walks up from the working folder to the first folder holding `.okf/`; the antigravity-harness ticket reuses the same launcher. Claude asks the user to approve a project `.mcp.json` server once; the install how-to says so.
- **`kmctl plugin install --harness claude`.** `--harness` takes a comma list; `claude` is the only value this ticket accepts (`antigravity` comes next). It runs `uvx --from apm-cli==0.33.0 apm install JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm#v<cli version> --target claude` in the repository, so the tag pinned to the CLI's own version keeps ADR 0001's promise that the CLI installs the content of its own release, then writes the hook. A failed APM run raises `PluginError` with APM's cause, as `_cause` does for claude today. `kmctl plugin update` re-runs the same steps. `kmctl plugin status` reports the ref recorded for the kmctl package in the repository's `apm.lock.yaml` against the CLI version, and whether the hook entry is present, each problem naming the command that fixes it; `--json` keeps working. The claude-marketplace code in `src/kmctl/plugin.py` (staging, `okf_source`, `extraKnownMarketplaces` handling, `claude plugin` calls) goes, with its tests (`tests/test_plugin_install.py`, `tests/test_plugin_error.py`, `tests/test_network_retry.py` where they test that code). The CLI's help (`src/kmctl/__init__.py`) and `docs/reference/commands.md` describe the new options.
- **`kmctl init` stops writing rules.** It no longer writes the 4 rules to `.claude/rules/`; they come from the package. That removes `_write_rules` and `RULE_FILES` from `src/kmctl/scaffold.py` and the rule-refresh half of `kmctl update` (the update-refreshes-rules ticket), and `tests/test_init.py` follows. Init's next step points at `kmctl plugin install`.
- **Other readers of `plugin/`.** `action.yml` and `.github/workflows/knowledge-audit.yml` set `KMCTL_PLUGIN_DIR` to `plugin`; `action/knowledge-audit.sh` reads the skills folder and the agent file under it, so both point at `apm/.apm` instead. `tests/test_audit.py`, `tests/test_skills.py`, `tests/test_briefing.py` and `tests/test_apm_package.py` read the new paths. This repository's own rules that scope to `plugin/**` (`.claude/rules/skills-are-thin.md`, `.claude/rules/skills-via-skill-creator.md`, `.claude/rules/adversarial-reviews.md`, `.claude/rules/cli-version-floor.md`, `.claude/rules/diagrams-stay-current.md`) get `apm/.apm/**` paths. This repository keeps its own adapted copies of the 4 rules in `.claude/rules/`.
- **Knowledge.** A new decision, made with `kmctl new decision`, records that APM is the only install route, wrapped by `kmctl plugin install --harness`, with the hook written by kmctl and the rules shipped in the package; `kmctl decision supersede` marks ADR 0013 (APM as a second route) and ADR 0003 (a Claude-only plugin) superseded, and the new record states which part of ADR 0011 (init writes the rules) it replaces, since ADR 0011's CLAUDE.md block and first decision stay. ADR 0001's consequence (the plugin is package data, staged) and ADR 0012's version source are corrected to name `apm/apm.yml`. `.okf/manifesto.md` (Parts, I1's test) and `.okf/architecture/overview.md` (its diagram and tables) say what the parts are now. `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md` gives `kmctl plugin install --harness claude`; `docs/how-to/install-kmctl-with-apm.md` says that a hand-added APM entry gets the skills, agent and rules but not the hook, and how to get it.
- **Tests.** The integration test in `tests/test_apm_package.py` (served git repository plus `uvx` `apm-cli==0.33.0`) is adapted to run `kmctl plugin install --harness claude` against the served tree and check what lands. Unit tests cover the settings merge: an existing `.claude/settings.json` with other hooks and keys keeps them, a second install leaves one kmctl entry, and an old kmctl entry is replaced in place.

Done when: in a scratch consumer repository with no kmctl content, `kmctl plugin install --harness claude` (against the served tree in the test, and against the release tag after it) leaves the 7 kmctl skills byte for byte in `.claude/skills/`, the auditor agent byte for byte in `.claude/agents/`, the 4 rules in `.claude/rules/` with `paths:` equal to today's, okf's skills, and exactly one briefing SessionStart entry in `.claude/settings.json`; `kmctl plugin status` there reports no problems; `plugin/` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` no longer exist; `scripts/release.py set` moves both apm.yml versions and the built wheel reports that version; and the gates pass.

Decided by the operator on 2026-10-16 (asked in session):

- **How the install names the package.** `kmctl plugin install` writes the kmctl dependency into the repository's `apm.yml` itself, as `{git: <source>, path: apm, ref: v<cli version>}`, and the harness list as `targets:`, then runs `apm install`. APM's CLI form cannot name a subfolder of a repository on a non-GitHub host (spike:apm-only-install/1), and APM records `targets:` in apm.yml only when it creates the file (spike:kmctl-doctor/1), so writing both entries makes the record doctor reads complete. A documented `--source GIT_URL` option (default `https://github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management.git`) points it elsewhere, for the integration test and for unreleased trees; it shows in `--help`. Operator's choice: an option, not an environment variable.
- **Old installs.** When `claude plugin list --json` shows `kmctl@kmctl` installed for this repository, `kmctl plugin install` uninstalls it (`claude plugin uninstall kmctl@kmctl --scope project`) and says so, so no skill loads twice. With `claude` not on PATH it skips that step. Operator's choice: remove, not just report. What happens to init-written rule copies follows risk 4.
- **`kmctl plugin status`.** It is folded into `kmctl doctor` in the kmctl-doctor ticket. This ticket keeps a working `plugin status` (lock ref against the CLI version, hook present) so nothing is broken in between; kmctl-doctor removes it.
- **User scope.** Kept only if risk 3's spike shows `apm install -g` delivers the package to the folder Claude Code reads at user scope; otherwise dropped (operator's choice). The spike showed it does, so `--scope user` stays.

## Could invalidate this plan

- Rule scoping: APM 0.33.0 might not carry the multi-glob `paths:` the 4 rules use (up to 6 globs, in `src/kmctl/repo_rules/diagrams-stay-current.md`) through `applyTo:`, so the rules would lose their scoping. Settled by spike:repo-uses-apm/3: a comma-joined `applyTo` of 6 globs (prompts-may-code-must) and of 2 (dependency-choice) landed in `.claude/rules/` as a `paths:` list equal to the globs, and bodies came through unchanged.
- Package layout: an `apm/apm.yml` with skills, agent and instructions under `apm/.apm/` and no `git: parent` might not deliver the agent byte for byte (ADR 0013 saw the agent dropped when an apm.yml sat beside agents outside `.apm/`), or `apm install <package> --target claude` might not work in a repository with no apm.yml of its own. Settled by spike:apm-only-install/1: the planned layout, served from a local git server and named in a consumer apm.yml as `{git, path: apm}`, installed with exit 0, all 7 skills and the agent byte for byte, the 4 rules with `paths:` equal to today's, and okf's skills; with no apm.yml, `apm install <tag> --target claude` created apm.yml and deployed. The CLI form cannot name a subfolder on a local host, which is why the install writes the apm.yml entry (above).
- User scope: with no `git: parent`, `apm install -g` might still refuse the package or write somewhere Claude Code does not read, which removes `--scope user` (the operator's fork above). Settled by spike:apm-only-install/2: `apm install -g` of a package with no `git: parent` exited 0, kept its state in `$HOME/.apm/`, and wrote skills, agent and rules (with `paths:`) under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (default `~/.claude/`), the folders Claude Code reads at user scope. So `--scope user` stays and runs `apm install -g`; the hook goes in the user settings file under the same folder. Tests must set both HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to scratch folders: an unrecorded run with only HOME redirected wrote into the real `~/.claude/`.
- Existing files: APM 0.33.0 might refuse, skip or silently overwrite a `.claude/rules/okf-bundle.md` (or a skill folder) it did not write, which every repository set up by `kmctl init` or the old plugin has. Skipping leaves stale rules with no warning; refusing breaks the install for every existing user. Spiked in spike:apm-only-install/3, and the risk is real for skills: APM overwrote a rule it did not write (`rewritten: .claude/rules/okf-bundle.md`), which is what replacing init's old copies needs, but left a skill folder it did not write in place, with `[!] 1 file skipped -- local files exist, not managed by APM`, and exited 0. The plan changes so the skip is never silent: `kmctl plugin install` greps APM's output for `skipped -- local files exist` and then fails with the skipped paths and the fix, `kmctl plugin install --force`, which passes `--force` to APM. Settled by spike:apm-only-install/5: the line is stable; APM never prints the path (plain, `-v` or `--dry-run`), so kmctl works it out by comparing the kmctl skill folders in the package with `deployed_files` in `apm.lock.yaml`; `--force` replaces the whole skill folder, deleting hand-made extra files, so the fix line warns that `--force` replaces those folders. Without `--force` kmctl never overwrites a file the user wrote. Who it touches: the old claude-plugin route kept skills in Claude's plugin cache, not `.claude/skills/`, and the ADR 0013 APM route's skills are APM-managed, so only a hand-made skill with a kmctl skill's name hits it.
